record.name: Saudi Arabia
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. The data and AI authority SDAIA issues AI risk and ethics frameworks; no model-evaluation institute run by it was found.

next_check.reason: Routine yearly re-check of a state where an institute is plausible (in Europe, the G20 or the OECD, or a signatory of the Bletchley Declaration).

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. The retrieved material does not sufficiently establish the national AI governance arrangements. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

Re-ran searches in English and Arabic for a government-designated institute that evaluates advanced models, or a commitment, proposal or study naming one. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified; results again described the draft Responsible AI Policy and SDAIA's work on the International AI Safety Report. Retrieved SDAIA's AI page as new primary governance evidence. Raised confidence to medium under the status-confidence rule: recorded queries in English and a national or official language, and cited primary governance evidence consistent with no qualifying institute. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

News search from 17 October 2026 in English and Arabic, with the SDAIA news listing (newest 4 November) and the communications ministry's homepage (newest 8 November). No qualifying item was found. Media-use principles and a foreign-ministers' session reported by Arab News and Saudi Gazette are neither a public advanced-model evaluator nor Network accession. The event detail pages of the Saudi Press Agency and SDAIA could not be read. Partial check, not a full record re-check.

Checked the note on the draft Responsible AI Policy against the policy text on the consultation platform, the official gazette's notice of 7 April 2026 and a law firm briefing of 4 November 2026, and bound it to them; it had been bound to an account of a different framework. The duties fall on all entities that release a high-risk system, which the note now says. Removed the outdated remark that SDAIA's AI page could not be read: it was retrieved on 24 October 2026. On 19 November 2026 the page refused the request again. Partial check, not a full record re-check.

check.governance_note: SDAIA's AI page describes the authority as the national reference body for regulating the data and AI sector, with an AI adoption framework, AI ethics principles and a national AI readiness index. It describes no model-evaluation institute.

related_bodies.name: SDAIA
related_bodies.role: It published a National AI Risk Management Framework in April 2026 that sets no model-testing rules. It is a national data and AI authority.

record.notes:
SDAIA put a draft Responsible AI Policy out for consultation until 3 May 2026. The draft lists human or automated red-team tests among the safety assessment methods SDAIA approves. It would require all entities to run comprehensive safety tests before releasing a high-risk system, with a safety report that covers regular checks for security vulnerabilities, and would put high-risk systems under annual audits by a third party accredited by SDAIA. The law firm AS&H Clifford Chance described the policy as still a draft on 4 November 2026.

Gowling's July 2026 account describes SDAIA's framework as governance guidance without performance benchmarks or model-testing rules. Searches covered indexed public English and Arabic sources for a government-designated AI safety institute with a remit to evaluate advanced models. SDAIA's own AI page describes the authority as the national reference body for data and AI and describes no model-evaluation institute.
